articles.title: Could caviar served on gourmet food tour of North Korea violate UN sanctions?
articles.excerpt: Russian tour company offers a tour of high-end Pyongyang restaurants inaccessible to average North Koreans.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean .
Caviar, wine, and foie gras served to Russian tourists in high-end Pyongyang restaurants is not necessarily evidence that exporters are violating sanctions that prohibit luxury items shipments to North Korea, but in the spirit of the sanctions these should be considered luxury items, a former member of the U.N. sanctions committee told Radio Free Asia.
Russian travel agency Vostok Intur is offering a gourmet tour that includes meals at many of the places frequented by North Korean elites: the twin-tower Koryo Hotel; the iconic Okryu-gwan restaurant, ground zero for Pyongyang’s high-class food culture; and a cruise ship sailing down the Taedong River which runs through the city.
The Russian Union of Travel Industry reported Monday that the travel company had completed its first gourmet tour with each participant paying roughly US$2,000 for the experience. The tour package includes an itinerary visiting restaurants inaccessible on standard tours, Inna Mukhina, the director of the travel agency, said in the report. The tour route and the restaurants are approved by North Korean tourism authorities, and it includes a stop at a restaurant called Rungra, where caviar and foie gras is served.
A table setting at a high-end Pyongyang restaurant, released by Vostok Intour, a travel agency based in Vladivostok, Russia.
(Vostok Intur) But whether this is a violation of sanctions depends on the interpretation of U.N. resolution 1718 – adopted by the U.N. Security Council in 2006 as a means to prevent the flow of cash and resources into North Korea’s nuclear missile programs. The resolution lists 14 luxury items that are banned for sale to North Korea, but caviar and foie gras are not among them.
The sanctions document should be viewed broadly rather than narrowly, Shuji Sue, a former member of the U.N. Panel of Experts on North Korea sanctions, told RFA Tuesday.
“Because the luxury goods are not specifically exemplified, this has always been a subject of debate when the panel of experts drafts reports,” he said. “I reiterate that I view caviar as a luxury item and consider it to be a luxury product prohibited by the Security Council.”
The European Union designates caviar and its substitutes as prohibited luxury goods, and the U.K., Japan, and Singapore also ban the export of caviar to North Korea. Wine is also subject to the luxury goods export ban by the E.U., the U.S., and the U.K.
Vostok Intur plans to regularize gourmet tourism starting in 2027, once a month with a maximum of 10 people per trip. According to the itinerary released on the agency’s website, tourists will visit the Koryo Hotel restaurant, the Hwasong Kumgang restaurant at the top of the Pyongyang Clock Tower, the Taedong River floating restaurant, and Okryu-gwan.
The price of next year’s group tour package announced by the travel agency is approximately $1,100, which includes a basic cost of 45,000 rubles (about $550) plus $550 for local accommodation expenses. Meal costs are calculated separately.
Even if the sanctions resolution is interpreted broadly, the caviar would not be a violation if it were produced domestically. RFA asked Vostok Intur about the source of the ingredients, but they did not respond.
Domestic production?
Though the source of the caviar has not been confirmed, North Korea has been farming sturgeon since the reign of Kim Jong Il, the father and predecessor of current leader Kim Jong Un. The state-run Korean Central News Agency reported in 2013 that the younger Kim visited a fish farm in South Hwanghae province, and said that his father’s last order before he died in 2011 was to raise as many sturgeon as possible so they could be prepared and served at Okryu-gwan.
This undated picture released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency on Feb. 21, 2017 shows North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un visiting the Samchon catfish farm in South Hwanghae Province, North Korea.
(KCNA via AFP) RFA was not able to confirm whether North Korea produces caviar domestically, but if it does, it can only be in small quantities, Lee Hyunseung, a former member of the North Korean elite whose family fled North Korea in 2014 and who now resides in the United States, told RFA.
“We cannot confirm the exact production volume, but as long as fish farms exist, domestic production is possible,” said Lee, who works as a senior researcher at the Maryland-based Global Peace Foundation. “However, mass production is not feasible. Clearly, if the number of tourists increases and tourism programs are operated more frequently, imports would be necessary to guarantee the required quantity.”
China is the world’s largest producer and exporter of sturgeon caviar but Beijing’s official export statistics show no record of the delicacy being sent to North Korea between 2018 and 2025. Russia, meanwhile, has not disclosed bilateral trade statistics since 2022, meaning that potentially Chinese caviar could enter North Korea via Russia.
Inequality exposed
The gourmet food tours are a stark contrast to the lifestyles of the typical resident of North Korea, a country that struggles with chronic food shortages, where a month’s salary cannot even buy a bag of rice.
Lee said that restaurants such as the Koryo Hotel or the Taedong River cruise ship can cost up to hundreds of dollars for a single meal, making them inaccessible to most people living in North Korea.
RFA reported last month that an average factory worker earns 20,000 North Korean won, about 30 US cents at the market exchange rate.
According to Vostok Intur’s itineraries, the tourists’ lunches and dinners are ordered and paid for separately, with an average cost of $20 per meal. This amount is equivalent to approximately five and a half times the average worker’s annual salary.
A group of Russian tourists arrive at the Pyongyang International Airport in Pyongyang, North Korea, Friday, Feb. 9, 2024.
(Cha Song Ho/AP) “ Russians travel to North Korea like this, pay $2,000, and enjoy a luxurious trip for three nights and four days,” said Lee. “I wonder how many people in North Korea can actually afford to pay $2,000 and enjoy that kind of luxury. Even the wealthy elites in the country simply cannot spend like that.”
According to South Korea’s Ministry of Unification, the cash-strapped North Korean government regards tourism as a key means of earning badly needed foreign currency.
“These tourism profits will also eventually be handed over to Kim Jong Un through the General Administration of National Tourism,” said Lee.
Edited by Yi Yongin in Korean and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: Foreign reporters enjoy their stays in Shenzhen
articles.excerpt: Media professionals gathered in Shenzhen for this year’s Apec meetings have had high praise for the city, hailing its technology…
articles.fullText:
Media professionals gathered in Shenzhen for this year’s Apec meetings have had high praise for the city, hailing its technology and people's hospitality.

Ekaterini Nicolaou from Cyprus, who is in China for the first time, said she was deeply touched by the hospitality of the locals.

"People are amazing and very hospitable. Even though we don't communicate in English, a lot of the time they're still very helpful and always there," she said.

"I feel very emotional to talk about this because Chinese people are impressive with their hospitality.

"We are in the subway, and somebody without you even asking them, they come to you and say, ‘Can I help you?’ and they don't take the train.'

She was also impressed by the humanoid robots showcased at the media centre, particularly those serving as TV hosts.

Sodas Salih from Iraq shared the same sentiment, saying he was impressed with the high-tech cameras showcased at the media centre.

"I think it’s like a letter from the Chinese government to tell the world that Shenzhen is special and Shenzhen is a capital of AI and technology, and they want the world to understand that Shenzhen is a special city," he said.

Alicia Boucher from Trinidad and Tobago was equally impressed by the China’s advancements in robotics.

"I have seen a lot of robots. My favourite, though, are humanoids," she said.

"I think it can be a great emotional support tool for a lot of people, the economic landscape, the cost of living."

Jarryl Bryan from Guyana, a coastal country in South America, was impressed by the amenities provided to help foreign reporters settle in.

"I've noticed that there are a lot of bilingual services, and I think it’s great. Everybody is accommodating all the foreign journalists here to cover Apec and so on,” he said.

The media centre also offers halal food and prayer rooms, alongside cleansing facilities in the washrooms for Muslim visitors.

According to Madiha Abid from Pakistan, the inclusion of halal options is a move that's very well thought-out.

"I think this is very sensitive, only a very considerate person could think like this. We have to respect the people who only eat halal, and they are offering a halal buffet. I'm very thankful to the management of Apec,” she said.

Diana Arushanyan from Armenia said she loved how China brought people from different cultural backgrounds together.

“I really love the idea that China is helping not only communicating with different cultures, but also making different cultures communicate with each other, and work to build something new,” she said.

Spanning 15,000 square metres, the media centre is capable of accommodating nearly 5,000 reporters.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Takaichi, Putin meet on Apec sidelines
articles.excerpt: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen in her…
articles.fullText:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen in her first face-to-face talks with the Russian president since she took office, Tokyo said on Thursday.

Relations between Tokyo and Moscow are at a low point after a Japanese journalist was arrested in Russia and assets of a Japanese tobacco firm were seized.

Takaichi "exchanged opinions with President Putin for about 30 minutes right after a welcome dinner party" on Wednesday, top government spokesman Minoru Kihara told reporters.

The Japanese premier conveyed Tokyo's positions on issues including the ongoing detention in Russia of a Japanese journalist arrested on spying allegations and the "protection of Japanese companies," Kihara said.

The Kremlin ordered this month the seizure of Japan Tobacco International's Russian assets, sparking an immediate protest from Tokyo.

The leaders agreed to "maintain communication at various levels", Kihara said.

The talks came a day after Japan lodged a protest with Moscow after suspected Russian aircraft entered its airspace, prompting Tokyo to scramble fighter jets.

Russia and Japan also have a decades-old dispute over the status of a string of islands in the Pacific Ocean.

In August, Japan protested Putin's visit to the far-eastern Kuril islands – a disputed territory known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.

Tokyo also protested in August against Russia's announcement that Moscow would conduct missile tests off one of the disputed islands visited by Putin. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK slips as Anthropic IPO to hold clue to AI sentiment
articles.excerpt: Asian equities were mixed and US stock futures rose on Thursday after Claude chatbot maker Anthropic scored the biggest initial…
articles.fullText:
Asian equities were mixed and US stock futures rose on Thursday after Claude chatbot maker Anthropic scored the biggest initial public offering ever with an US$81 billion offering ahead of its market debut in a test for the artificial intelligence trade that has been under pressure in recent weeks.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down 245 points, or 1.05 percent, at 23,049.

The China enterprises index slid 74 points, or 0.95 percent, to 7,762 while the tech index fell 36 points, or 0.97 percent, to 3,699.

Higher north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index inched down four points, or 0.13 percent, to open at 3,583.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 67 points, or 0.63 percent, to 10,591 while the ChiNext Index was down 0.93 percent at 2,290.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened less than a point up at 59,025 and was 136 points higher at one stage before lunch.

In Seoul, the Kospi rose 22 points, or 0.45 percent, to open at 5,090 before reversing direction to be 67 points lower at one stage before lunch.

On a fully diluted basis, Anthropic's IPO values the large language model maker, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about US$1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing.

"I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI. I think much of that boils down to future investment growth... However, if the stock trades the way it looks like it will, it might calm the market a bit."

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken in the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build AI infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia this week as uncertainty caused by chief executive Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of an interest rate hike in December.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

The comments come after hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, leaving markets bracing for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90 percent chance of a 25 basis points hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD." (Agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: China pledges US$20m to boost Apec cooperation: Xi
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Thursday called on leaders attending the Apec summit in Shenzhen to build an Asia-Pacific community that…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Thursday called on leaders attending the Apec summit in Shenzhen to build an Asia-Pacific community that features solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, innovation, and inclusive development.

Xi said China will provide US$20 million to support regional cooperation at the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting, as he announced a series of measures to consistently support cooperation across the Asia-Pacific.

These include the establishment of a centre for Asia-Pacific community studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support.

The president said China will also set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, contributing to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific.

Xi also stressed the need to steadily advance economic integration in the region, and called on members to facilitate free, open trade and investment, unclog bottlenecks and ensure smooth economic circulation.

He emphasised the importance of innovation in building an Asia-Pacific community, saying it is imperative to encourage exchanges and cooperation on the sci-tech front, facilitate the utilisation of innovation outcomes, and foster a cooperation environment that is open, fair, just and non-discriminatory.

Xi added that the bond of shared interests among Apec members should be strengthened, and they should work together to tackle difficulties and challenges, and continue to foster a sense of community.

Efforts should be made to ensure that the benefits of development are shared by all, he said.

China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, Xi added, saying China is ready to work with all parties to build the pillars that support an Asia-Pacific community. (Reporting by Xinhua)

articles.title: Van Gogh work fetches record price after owner dispute
articles.excerpt: A Vincent van Gogh masterpiece sold for a record-breaking US$190.4 million after a dispute between the seller and the heirs…
articles.fullText:
A Vincent van Gogh masterpiece sold for a record-breaking US$190.4 million after a dispute between the seller and the heirs of a previous Jewish owner who sold it in the Nazi era, Sotheby's said.

"Chataigniers en fleurs" (Chestnut Trees in Blossom) painted in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, France set a new record for the Dutch post-Impressionist and became the most expensive work auctioned off so far this season.

The previous auction record for a painting by Van Gogh was US$117.2 million for the 1888 "Orchard with Cypresses" at Christie's in New York in November 2022.

An influential German publisher, Samuel Fischer, acquired the painting in Paris in 1909 and his family sold it in 1936.

His heirs had previously opposed the sale, saying Fischer's family parted with the painting only because of financial losses suffered under the Nazis.

The heirs' Berlin-based lawyer, Gunnar Schnabel, had called on Sotheby's to prove the painting was sold at its market value and that the family would have sold it regardless of the political context.

The Blaquier-Arrieta family acquired the painting in 1975 and has owned it for more than half a century, according to Sotheby's.

But on Tuesday, Sotheby's said: "An agreement has been reached between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and all of the legal descendants of Hedwig and Samuel Fischer regarding the sale of Vincent van Gogh's Chataigniers en fleurs."

Schnabel did not respond to an AFP request for comment.

According to Sotheby's, the Fischer heirs said they were "grateful for the trusting and fair negotiation and collaboration with Sotheby's and the Blaquier-Arrieta family, which make it possible to acknowledge the suffering of the Fischer family during the Nazi era and honour Gisela Berman Fischer's history of seeking justice for her family." (AFP)

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: Cummins defiant amid fresh 'Sandpapergate' claims
articles.excerpt: Pat Cummins remained defiant on Thursday as his position as Australia Test captain was called into question after he was…
articles.fullText:
Pat Cummins remained defiant on Thursday as his position as Australia Test captain was called into question after he was dragged back into the "Sandpapergate" scandal by Cameron Bancroft's explosive revelations.

Bancroft, a central figure in the 2018 ball-tampering plot in South Africa that rocked world cricket, dropped a grenade late Wednesday in a lengthy newspaper column by claiming the whole team knew what was going on.

It came just days after Cummins held a 70-minute press conference to rebut the same allegations by Usman Khawaja in his autobiography, calling them "100 percent wrong".

Bancroft was the player who used sandpaper during a Test in Cape Town to make the ball swing, with a Cricket Australia probe concluding only he, then-skipper Steve Smith and his deputy David Warner were responsible.

They were all sent home in disgrace and banned.

In a statement to several Australian media outlets, Cummins' manager Neil Maxwell said: "Pat's position hasn't changed in eight years. He's been consistent and adamant from day one.

"Pat feels for Cam of course. He has been through a lot. We would urge people to again read Pat's interview transcript. There is nothing he hasn't answered. And that includes in response to what Cam has now said.

"Pat has rebuilt the Australian cricket team. That 24-year-old in Cape Town resolved to fix the team and spent eight years doing it," he added.

Despite the defiance, calls are mounting for his position to be reviewed.

"Pat Cummins' future as Test captain should be placed under immediate review after Cameron Bancroft's stunning accusation that the skipper didn't tell us the truth," The Australian newspaper said in an opinion piece.

"Cummins' press conference in Sydney last week when he forcefully denied any knowledge of the plot to use sandpaper in a Test in 2018 could become the worst strategic move of his career."

National broadcaster ABC agreed with the sentiment, saying "his position as captain of the Australian Test team is now questionable", while the Sydney Morning Herald stated: "Cummins' captaincy in peril".

The naming of Australia's squad for their home Test series against New Zealand in December-January was expected this week, but has now been pushed back.

Hours before Bancroft's revelations, Cricket Australia said it would not reopen its investigation but instead set up a forum for players to share their experiences about 2018.

Chief executive Todd Greenberg also declared Cummins' version of events was not under scrutiny.

"No, the captain doesn't need to be cleared. No-one's looking to be cleared," Greenberg said.

Bancroft had suggested in a 2021 interview the bowling group, including Cummins, knew about the scheme.

In response, Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly they were aware of the plan.

Starc reiterated his stance last week. Hazlewood and Lyon have yet to comment. Neither has Smith.

Bancroft said he felt "angry and betrayed" by Cummins' denials.

"It was not just the three of us. Steve Smith, David Warner and I knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa. It was the whole team," he wrote.

"The final straw for me to write this account was Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins's press conference."

In other revelations, Bancroft claimed Warner first raised the prospect of using sandpaper during the second Test at Port Elizabeth and coaches Darren Lehmann and David Saker were "certainly present" during talks about the issue.

Lehmann, who quit in the days after Cape Town, has continuously denied knowing anything.

Speaking on ABC radio during the third Australia-England one-dayer in Hobart on Wednesday, he said he would take time to work through Bancroft's allegations.

"It's only just come to light. I just need to sit back and process all that and work through each allegation," he said. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Alcaraz reaches ATP Finals semis with help from Tiafoe
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz reached the last four of the ATP Finals on Wednesday thanks to Frances Tiafoe after the Spaniard had…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz reached the last four of the ATP Finals on Wednesday thanks to Frances Tiafoe after the Spaniard had earlier brushed aside world number five Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4.

American Tiafoe beat Italian Flavio Cobolli 7-6 (8/6), 6-0 with his first set guaranteeing Alcaraz's spot in the next round.

Tiafoe kept his hopes of a semi-final spot alive in his maiden Finals appearance and faces Medvedev in his last group-stage match on Friday.

Seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz needed just over 70 minutes to beat the Russian in Turin.

"A little bit of problems, you know, physically, in the match," Alcaraz said on-court after receiving some treatment in the second set.

"But I think everybody could see that I was able to still play good tennis, I could still move well."

By winning in straight sets, the 23-year-old will secure his spot in the semi-finals if Frances Tiafoe defeats Flavio Cobolli later or if the Italian beats the American in three sets.

Alcaraz has never won the season-ending Finals, finishing runner-up last year to Jannik Sinner.

But with Sinner injured and the Spaniard entering this season's edition on the back of a nine-match winning streak that earned him indoor titles in Vienna and at the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is considered the favourite to lift the trophy this year.

Since returning in August from a wrist injury that kept him off the tour for four months and prevented him from defending his French Open title, Alcaraz has won three of the five tournaments he has entered.

After easing past Tiafoe in his opener in Turin 6-2, 6-2, the third seed carried that ominous form into the first set against 2020 Finals winner Medvedev.

Alcaraz broke the Russian in successive games midway through the first frame to claim the opener.

He continued by breaking Medvedev in the very first game of the second set and proceeded to serve out, despite a brief stoppage to have his left thigh taped up.

"I didn't want to force myself to the limit physically. I was a break-up at that time. And I just tried to keep up my serve... play chill, smoothly, relaxed and just happy about it," Alcaraz said.

"So, I'm going to look at it with my team and I will see."

Medvedev, 30, is still in with a chance of advancing after winning his opening match against Cobolli in straight sets.

World number one Alexander Zverev is the man to beat in the John McEnroe Group and became the first player to book his spot in the semi-finals after beating Ben Shelton on Tuesday. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Hegseth announces military partnership with Venezuela
articles.excerpt: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new agreement on military cooperation with Venezuela on Wednesday as he made his…
articles.fullText:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new agreement on military cooperation with Venezuela on Wednesday as he made his first visit to the country since US special forces deposed President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid in Caracas.

Hegseth announced the agreement alongside acting President Delcy Rodriguez, who welcomed him to the presidential palace. He said it covered joint training, intelligence sharing and other aspects of US-Venezuelan military cooperation. Rodriguez said the arrangement would help confront "common threats" and strengthen training for Venezuela's armed forces.

Hegseth said the partnership would herald a significant ramp-up in joint action against drug trafficking groups.

"To the narco terrorists who have used this as a safe haven, your time is up. We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you," Hegseth said, speaking from the US embassy.

Washington already holds growing influence in Venezuela, particularly in the oil sector. Since Maduro's removal, US officials have moved quickly to shape the country's future, focusing on energy policy and investment.

That role expanded sharply in August under a deal granting producer North American Blue Energy Partners, or NABEP, long-term access to 17 oilfields that contain about a fifth of the country's oil reserves through a partnership with the US government. The United States secured a 35 percent stake in NABEP's parent, a guaranteed share of output and first refusal rights on the remainder.

Hegseth's trip to Venezuela came two weeks after voter anger over the Iran war helped drive an election defeat for US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in Congress. The unpopular, nearly nine-month-old conflict has driven up gasoline prices in the US and around the world, as Iran fires on tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz off its coast.

Hegseth, who has defended the Iran war as courageous, said the oil deal with Venezuela "makes the Strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the Western Hemisphere."

Alejandro Betancourt, the Venezuelan businessman who controls NABEP and was central to the agreement, told reporters he discussed the progress of oil cooperation with Hegseth, adding that NABEP plans to produce over 250,000 barrels per day of oil by year-end as it prepares to have 10 well clusters in service.

That would be an increase from the 224,000 bpd it produced in mid-October, according to company figures.

Hegseth's Caracas stop came at the start of a trip to Latin America. He was expected in Colombia on Wednesday to deliver military equipment and discuss security cooperation with Bogota.

Colombia's defense minister said Hegseth was due to hand over a Lockheed Martin Hercules C-130 aircraft and discuss US support as Colombia battles drug trafficking groups and other illegal armed actors.

In August, Hegseth floated the possibility of joint strikes on Colombian armed groups.

Trump's Latin America policy has expanded dramatically beyond its early focus on the Panama Canal. More than 200 people have been killed since the launch of US military ⁠strikes on suspected drug boats last year.

As he addressed the gathering in Caracas, Hegseth invoked a revamped Monroe Doctrine, the 19th-century policy asserting US primacy across the Americas that critics associate with decades of US intervention.

He called it the "Donroe Doctrine" – a play on Trump's name.

"That is the Donroe Doctrine. Venezuela has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner on its way to rebuilding its military alongside the United States," Hegseth said. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Anthropic prices blockbuster IPO at US$83 per share
articles.excerpt: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at US$83 per share on Wednesday, according to multiple reports, an amount above the…
articles.fullText:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at US$83 per share on Wednesday, according to multiple reports, an amount above the expected price range that values the artificial intelligence giant at US$1.5 trillion.

The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool is set to make its debut on Wall Street on Thursday. The company had set a price range of US$70 to US$78 per share, offering 825 million shares that will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

The company is also selling another US$26 billion of stock in a private placement.

Anthropic decided to barrel ahead with the IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led US Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public.

Anthropic already has taken on US$6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial.” Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting its resources are limited to pay interest and principal.

While the company has ample cash for now, it will likely run through it quickly if it cannot raise more soon, given its outsized spending plans. The company said it has already signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend US$900 billion on computing power and infrastructure in the coming years, including US$70 billion in the next 12 months.

Anthropic's IPO also means its employees can begin to sell their vested stock, a payout that will make many of them millionaires. The IPO could also give Anthropic enormous resources to accelerate its expansion and potentially add billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela Amodei.

Formed in 2021 by former OpenAI leaders, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company. But both companies have plenty of other competitors, including Google, startups in the US and China and SpaceX, which has an AI business.

Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all lost more money than they’ve made because of the huge costs associated with building AI. That has fuelled growing concerns about a bubble forming in the AI sector.

Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned that AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months.

Amid those fears, the regulatory environment could also change for Anthropic once the new US Congress is in session. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry amid a national backlash against data centres, giving new impetus to a congressional effort last year to enact a national moratorium on new ones.

And two big states offering incentives for data centres, Texas and Georgia, just elected Democratic governors vowing to stop new construction.

Adding to the pressure is the possibility that demand for AI shares could drop or even collapse. Investors have become anxious about the massive financing needs of the sector, and several tech companies have pulled IPO plans recently. OpenAI is not planning to go public until next year. (AP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' launches to rave reviews
articles.excerpt: Gamers around the world got their first taste of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on…
articles.fullText:
Gamers around the world got their first taste of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever.

The latest instalment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time.

The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalised US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs.

"GTA VI" launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight.

New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. "Wasted already. First one, didn't survive long," he told AFP, laughing.

"This is one of the big things in my life... I've been playing GTA for such a long time," Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP.

Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100.

Analytics firm Omdia estimates "GTA VI" could generate US$3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive.

PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored.

In a review for The Verge titled "GTA VI does something impossible – it lives up to the hype," Andrew Webster wrote that "the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it."

Social media users praised the graphics.

"There's one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human," wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652.

Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University's Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an "outlier" in the entertainment industry.

"This is the Taylor Swift of video games," he said.

"The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services," such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter.

Many fans have taken time off to explore the fictional state of Leonida, which is modelled on Florida.

"I'm going to take four days off," said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning his first session "for a very long time."

Human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests worldwide for November 19.

Billed as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, "GTA VI" follows a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in Vice City, a crime-ridden city modelled on Miami.

The game received eight nominations on Tuesday for the Game Awards, the US ceremony honouring the year's best video games, which takes place on December 10.

Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the game.

The studio delayed the launch twice after a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online, and it was hit by another round of leaks last summer.

The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime. It has also become a pop culture symbol of subversion, known for mocking the flaws of American society. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: 'Most Fed policymakers think more rate hikes likely'
articles.excerpt: "Almost all" participants of the US Federal Reserve's interest rate-setting meeting in October thought that further rate hikes would be…
articles.fullText:
"Almost all" participants of the US Federal Reserve's interest rate-setting meeting in October thought that further rate hikes would be necessary to fight stubbornly high inflation, minutes of the meeting showed on Wednesday.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labour market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate... would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the two percent objective," the minutes, released after a customary three-week lag, said.

The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at its last meeting in late October, even as its Chairman Kevin Warsh said inflation remained "too high."

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00 percent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

Two voting members, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, had dissented in favour of an immediate 25-basis-point hike.

The Fed has a dual mandate of keeping inflation to its target while ensuring maximum employment.

The unemployment rate in the United States has been relatively steady over the last year, even as job growth has see-sawed. That stability is due to demographic changes and lower immigration.

Inflation, on a downward trajectory since hitting a pandemic peak, has reignited in the last year, driven by US President Donald Trump's tariff policies and the energy price spike caused by his war on Iran.

Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, hit 3.6 percent in September, far above the Fed's long-term two-percent target. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wall Street ends mixed after Nvidia earnings
articles.excerpt: US stocks were mixed on Wednesday as investors digested Nvidia results and Anthropic priced its initial public offering, while weighing…
articles.fullText:
US stocks were mixed on Wednesday as investors digested Nvidia results and Anthropic priced its initial public offering, while weighing hawkish sentiment reflected in US Federal Reserve minutes.

After gyrating early in the session, the Nasdaq closed modestly higher, the Dow ended sharply lower, and the S&P 500 reversed its modest gains to settle in negative territory following the Fed minutes release.

Nvidia's quarterly results released late on Tuesday beat analyst expectations, and the AI chipmaker forecast quarterly revenue above estimates. Even so, its shares fell 2.9 percent amid uncertainties caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure last week.

Anthropic priced its IPO at US$83 a share, above its targeted range of US$70 to US$78 per share, in one of the largest stock market IPOs on record and the first by a major frontier AI model developer, according to a person familiar with the matter. Bloomberg News first reported the pricing.

Other chipmakers were mixed. Intel dropped 0.9 percent, Micron dipped 1 percent, but Advanced Micro Devices gained 5.3 percent.

"There's been a lot of dark clouds of uncertainty over technology, chip stocks and AI in general," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. "It's important to remember the market's not totally falling apart here. It clearly is top-heavy with tech, but there are other groups that are actually doing pretty well under the surface."

Target jumped 4 percent after the discount retailer provided an upbeat holiday outlook. Results from its larger rival Walmart are expected on Thursday.

TJX surged 8 percent after forecasting strong annual sales, banking on high demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Take-Two Interactive shares rose 6.2 percent ahead of the rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game.

On the sector level, consumer discretionary was a clear outperformer, with a boost from a 3.8 percent gain in Amazon shares.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 561 points, or 1.1 percent, to 50,198, the S&P 500 lost 16 points, or 0.2 percent, to 7,323 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 101 points, or 0.4 percent, to 24,429.

Minutes from the Fed's October policy meeting showed the central bank remained focused on inflation risks, recognising the need for further rate hikes if the economy progresses as expected. A few policymakers argued the case for a 50-basis-point rate hike "if incoming inflation data were unfavourable."

Consumer and producer price data released after the October meeting showed hotter-than-expected price growth.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller took a hawkish stance on Wednesday, saying the central bank needs to be more aggressive in responding to inflation. This follows John Williams' comments on Tuesday, in which the New York Fed president said that while he favours tighter monetary policy, there was no need for "dramatic action."

Financial markets are pricing in a near-certain probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the conclusion of the Fed's December meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"Inflation continues to be stubbornly higher than anyone wants," Detrick said. "The Fed's going to probably do a 25-basis-point hike in December, and a couple more hikes early next year is a very real possibility." (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Jeffries set to be first black speaker of US House
articles.excerpt: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats…
articles.fullText:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader on Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.

The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media.

Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power.

His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of US President Donald Trump's term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration.

Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday's election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination "by acclamation" – without a formal ballot – as some allies had hoped.

He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018.

The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous.

Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party's plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.

"Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one," he told reporters on Tuesday.

"We're going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America."

Raised in Brooklyn's working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.

He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump's first impeachment trial in 2020.

As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington's most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.

But he would face a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

Jeffries's nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.

Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Rohingya hope for justice as UN court prepares to rule on Myanmar genocide case
articles.excerpt: An activist who fled Myanmar’s 2017 military crackdown says a historic ruling must lead to real change for refugees
articles.fullText:
A Rohingya activist who fled Myanmar as a teenager hopes a landmark ruling by the United Nations’ highest court on Thursday will bring long-awaited recognition of her community’s suffering, she told Radio Free Asia.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague is set to rule Nov. 19 on whether Myanmar violated the 1948 Genocide Convention during a military crackdown against the predominantly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, which forced more than 730,000 people to flee to neighboring Bangladesh.
Though she hopes for a favorable ruling, Lucky Karim, a Rohingya who escaped the violence at the age of 14 and is now a human rights activist, warned that justice will mean little without action to protect refugees and allow them to return home.
“For Rohingya to have a positive outcome, it will be a historic moment, a historic victory for us,” she told RFA, adding that such a ruling could also offer hope to other ethnic minority communities in Myanmar, where years of conflict and military repression have displaced millions of people.
Lucky Karim, in front row on the left, with classmates at a primary school in Hlaing Thi village, Maungdaw Township, Rakhine State.
(Lucky Karim) Originally from Hlaing Thi village in Rakhine State’s Maungdaw township, Karim spent six years in a refugee camp in Bangladesh. In 2022, she founded Refugee Women for Peace and Justice, an organization advocating for the rights and education of Rohingya women.
Her hopes reflect the significance of a case that has taken seven years to reach a judgment and could establish Myanmar’s legal responsibility for one of the worst episodes of mass displacement in recent decades.
What happened to the Rohingya?
The Rohingya are a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority from Myanmar’s western Rakhine State who have faced decades of discrimination, restrictions on movement and denial of citizenship in the Buddhist-majority country.
In August 2017, Myanmar’s military launched what it described as clearance operations after Rohingya militants attacked security posts. Soldiers were accused of killing civilians, raping women and burning entire villages, driving hundreds of thousands of people across the border into Bangladesh.
A United Nations fact-finding mission later concluded that there were reasonable grounds to infer genocidal intent behind the military campaign and called for senior military officials to be investigated and prosecuted.
Myanmar has rejected accusations of genocide, maintaining that its operations were legitimate responses to attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, a Rohingya insurgent group.
The Gambia, a small West African nation, brought the case against Myanmar in November 2019 with the backing of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.
It accused Myanmar of violating the Genocide Convention, an international treaty adopted after World War II that obliges countries to prevent and punish genocide.
A view of the Great Hall of Justice, the courtroom of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, June 18, 2026. (Nicolas Economou/Reuters)
(Reuters) The ICJ ordered Myanmar in January 2020 to take measures to prevent genocidal acts against the Rohingya and preserve evidence.
Myanmar’s government filed objections to the case in January 2021, just days before the country’s military took control of the country in a coup.
The court rejected the objections in 2022, and held hearings on the allegations in January this year.
During those hearings, The Gambia argued that the pattern of killings, sexual violence and destruction demonstrated an intent to destroy the Rohingya as a group. Myanmar’s military government disputed that interpretation, arguing that the evidence did not meet the legal threshold required to establish genocide.
What could the ruling change?
Thursday’s judgment will determine whether Myanmar bears responsibility under international law for violations of the Genocide Convention.
Unlike the International Criminal Court, which prosecutes individuals, the ICJ settles disputes between countries. Its ruling cannot directly send military commanders to prison or compel the immediate return of refugees.
But a finding against Myanmar would carry legal and diplomatic weight and could require the country to take further measures to address violations and provide reparations.
For Karim, the distinction between a legal victory and improvements in refugees’ lives is crucial.
“The judgment from the International Court of Justice does not immediately change the ground reality. It doesn’t immediately repatriate refugees from refugee camps to Burma either,” she said, using Myanmar’s former name.
The challenges facing the Rohingya have only deepened since the 2017 crackdown.
After the 2021 coup, the country was plunged into a wider civil war. Renewed fighting in Rakhine State between the military and the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group, has exposed Rohingya civilians to further violence and displacement.
The United Nations said in May that approximately 150,000 Rohingya had arrived in Bangladesh since early 2024, adding to the pressure on already overcrowded refugee settlements.
Around 1.2 million Rohingya refugees were living in Bangladesh, according to the UN’s May estimate, most of them in and around Cox’s Bazar, home to one of the world’s largest refugee settlements.
Their return to Myanmar remains fraught with uncertainty, with concerns over safety, citizenship rights and protection from persecution still unresolved.
Lucky Karim is seen in front of the house where he lived in refugee camp number 8 in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, in March 2019.
(Lucky Karim) “Until it is safe for everyone, it’s not safe for any one of us in Burma,” Karim said.
She urged governments and international organizations to ensure that any judgment leads to concrete measures to protect refugees and create conditions for their safe, voluntary and dignified return.
The ICJ’s judgments are legally binding, although the court has no independent enforcement force. If a country fails to comply, the other party may seek action through the UN Security Council.
Karim said achieving lasting change would require sustained international commitment and the implementation of the court’s ruling, rather than simply recognizing the atrocities committed against the Rohingya.
“So the judgment should not be a piece of paper,” she said. “It shouldn’t be another genocide declaration.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin summit puts nuclear arms control, North Korea in focus
articles.excerpt: Analysts see little prospect of a nuclear deal, while Pyongyang hopes its allies will press its case with the US.
articles.fullText:
When U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC summit , a concrete agreement on nuclear arms control would be an unlikely result, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
The meeting comes as Washington seeks to bring Beijing into nuclear discussions with Moscow, while China maintains that its smaller arsenal makes participation in such negotiations unreasonable. North Korea, meanwhile, is closely monitoring the meeting for any implications it might have for its own nuclear weapons program.
Though a deal is not likely, the summit could open channels for further consultations on nuclear risks, Cheng Xiaonong, a U.S.-based Chinese scholar, told RFA Mandarin.
“My understanding is that Trump is essentially trying to use Putin to teach Xi Jinping a lesson,” he said. “Of course, Putin will want to negotiate something in return.”
U.S. President Donald Trump shakes hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China’s President Xi Jinping stands beside, before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 18, 2026.
(Iori Sagisawa/Reuters) Trump is scheduled to meet Xi bilaterally before joining Putin for trilateral talks. Discussions are expected to include nuclear disarmament or the wars in Ukraine and Iran, although China has not released a detailed agenda.
North Korea, which maintains close ties with both Beijing and Moscow, has not publicly commented on the summit, but analysts say Pyongyang may hope its allies will use the meeting to advance its longstanding demands for recognition as a nuclear-armed state and relief from international sanctions.
Competing nuclear interests
The United States and Russia have decades of experience negotiating nuclear arms control agreements, but China has resisted joining similar negotiations, arguing that its nuclear arsenal remains substantially smaller.
Cheng said that China’s continued nuclear expansion and reliance on strategic deterrence would make a trilateral agreement difficult.
He said Washington would seek a commitment from Xi to restrain China’s nuclear arsenal, while Beijing and Moscow would pursue their own objectives in negotiations with Trump.
“All three have their own calculations, and they can’t work together,” Cheng said. “Under those circumstances, a joint statement would be meaningless.”
Spectators wave Chinese flags as military vehicles carrying DF-41 nuclear ballistic missiles roll during a parade to commemorate the 70th anniversary of the founding of Communist China in Beijing, Oct. 1, 2019.
(Mark Schiefelbein/AP) Xi will likely use the summit to demonstrate China’s status as a major power and strengthen his domestic political authority, Song Guocheng, a Taiwanese international relations scholar, told RFA Mandarin.
He also considered a concrete nuclear arms control agreement unlikely but said the leaders could still make progress on reducing nuclear risks.
The leaders “could establish what we call a nuclear weapons communication mechanism, with emergency procedures or arrangements between them,” Song said. “That could at least help prevent nuclear miscalculations.”
China’s Foreign Ministry said Monday that the leaders would exchange views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability among major powers.
Beijing has previously said requiring China to participate in trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage would be neither reasonable nor realistic.
North Korea seeks recognition, fears concessions
For North Korea, analysts say the summit could provide an opportunity to seek diplomatic support for its nuclear ambitions, although Pyongyang is not participating in the talks.
North Korea likely hopes that China and Russia will convey Pyongyang’s demands to Trump, Kim Tae-woo, a former president of the Seoul-based Korea Institute for National Unification, told RFA Korean.
“North Korea essentially has two demands and expectations when it comes to nuclear weapons,” Kim said. “The first is recognition of its status as a nuclear-armed state. The second is that any nuclear talks with the United States must be conducted as arms reduction negotiations between nuclear powers on an equal footing.”
Analysts said an explicit endorsement of North Korea’s nuclear status was unlikely, but the absence of calls for denuclearization could still be welcomed by Pyongyang.
This image distributed by the North Korean government on March 24, 2022, and not independently verifiable shows leader Kim Jong Un walking away from what state media reports as a "new type" of intercontinental ballistic missile.
(KCNA via Reuters) “North Korea will hope that there are no statements about stability on the Korean Peninsula or North Korea’s denuclearization,” Shin Beom-chul, South Korea’s former vice minister of national defense, told RFA Korean. “They will be satisfied as long as denuclearization is not discussed.”
North Korea may also hope Beijing and Moscow will press Washington to ease sanctions, analysts said.
In December 2017, the U.N. Security Council – which includes Russia and China – adopted Resolution 2397, which imposed tighter restrictions on North Korea’s petroleum supplies, exports and overseas workers.
The summit could present risks for Pyongyang if China or Russia uses their relationships with North Korea as leverage.
Recent high-level diplomatic exchanges between North Korea and its neighbors might be showing Pyongyang’s concerns about being sidelined, Ko Young-hwan, a former president of South Korea’s National Institute for Unification Education, told RFA Korean.
“The war in Ukraine won’t go on forever,” Ko said. “North Korea is probably worried that China and Russia might do something with the United States behind its back.”
South Korea’s presidential office has said Seoul’s position and interests must be fully reflected in discussions among the three powers.
Prospects for further talks
Beyond nuclear arms control, analysts differ on whether the summit could lead to a more permanent diplomatic framework among Washington, Beijing and Moscow.
A scholar of U.S.-China relations identified only as Mr. Xing told RFA Mandarin that the meeting could signal the emergence of a “new Yalta system,” referring to the 1945 conference at which Allied leaders discussed the postwar international order.
Members of the "Art Lift" collective carry the artwork showing U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping next to the 'Big Three' monument with the leaders at the 1945 Yalta conference - Joseph Stalin, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill, in Livadia park in Yalta, Crimea, Nov. 16, 2026.
(Alexey Pavlishak/Reuters) Xing predicted the summit would remain largely symbolic, with China unlikely to support a formal consultation mechanism.
The U.S.-based Arms Control Association said ahead of the meeting that a single summit was unlikely to produce a major breakthrough, but the leaders could instruct negotiating teams to begin sustained discussions on nuclear arms limits and risk reduction.
The Kremlin said the parties were discussing a possible joint communiqué. If they cannot agree on a text, the three leaders will issue separate assessments of the talks.
Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.

articles.title: HK IP Academy launches
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan today attended the opening ceremony of the 16th Business of Intellectual Property (IP) Asia Forum, during…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today attended the opening ceremony of the 16th Business of Intellectual Property (IP) Asia Forum, during which the Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy was officially launched.

A major IP conference, the forum is being held over two days at the Convention & Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai.

Speaking at the forum, Mr Chan said the National 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre.

Launched in partnership with the Monetary Authority last December, the IP Financing Sandbox has so far seen banks approve seven loans.

Mr Chan highlighted that the task now is to move from "sandbox to scale".

“Banks, valuers and borrowers are discovering together what makes IP bankable," he said. "The next phase of the initiative will draw in more participants. And a new pilot scheme will help smaller firms obtain professional valuations of their patents, in line with the national standard.

“An agreement is only as reliable as its enforcement, so IP disputes can be settled here in Hong Kong by arbitration or mediation, under a bilingual common law system that international parties know well.”

The Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy was jointly established by the Intellectual Property Department and the Vocational Training Council.

The Government earmarked $52 million in the 2026-27 Budget to support the academy's establishment and its first two years of operation. It is expected to provide training for around 2,000 participants over the two-year pilot period.

Speaking at the academy’s opening ceremony, Acting Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Bernard Chan remarked that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan sets out the establishment of an IP academy to systematically nurture talent for IP-intensive industries, equipping practitioners with knowledge and skills spanning IP creation, protection, management, financing, utilisation and commercialisation.

To support innovation and technology, as well as the business, professional services, cultural and creative sectors, the academy will establish a multilevel on-the-job training pathway, and develop certified courses and Qualifications Framework-recognised programmes.

The academy's first foundation course is being held today and tomorrow during the forum.

articles.title: CE joins APEC leaders’ meeting
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today attended the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. He exchanged views…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today attended the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. He exchanged views with regional leaders on deepening co-operation and expanding into diversified markets.

Speaking at the meeting, Mr Lee remarked that the Asia-Pacific region is today’s economic growth engine, accounting for two-thirds of global growth. He said that as an international finance, trade and innovation centre that benefits from national support, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region will give full play to its strengths as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”. Hong Kong, he added, will continue to maintain a free and open market, embrace the rules-based multilateral trading system, and expand its co-operation with APEC to contribute to the region’s development and prosperity.

Mr Lee outlined that the Greater Bay Area is a key platform for open co-operation and high-quality development. He said that hosting the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, after Hong Kong hosted the APEC Finance Ministers’ Meeting for the first time last month, underscores the bay area’s international relevance and competitiveness. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster has ranked top globally for two consecutive years in the Global Innovation Index of innovation clusters, reflecting mutually beneficial co-operation on innovation and technology among sister cities in the bay area.

APEC member economies reached a consensus on today’s Leaders’ Declaration, and adopted leader-level outcome documents on trade digitalisation, the digital economy, emerging technologies, and connectivity. Mr Lee said these forward-looking outcomes play a crucial role in advancing practical co-operation in the Asia-Pacific, deepening regional economic integration and promoting high-quality development.

In the afternoon, Mr Lee held bilateral meetings with leaders of other economies. During his meeting with President of Peru Keiko Fujimori, Mr Lee recalled witnessing the signing of a Free Trade Agreement between Hong Kong and Peru in Lima in 2024. The agreement officially entered into force on September 1 this year, further boosting bilateral trade and investment and marking a new milestone in economic and trade relations between the two places.

He urged Peruvian enterprises to make good use of Hong Kong’s international trading platform and professional services, and to use Hong Kong as a springboard to enter the Mainland and wider Asian markets to capture new business opportunities. He added that Hong Kong will continue to expand into emerging markets, leverage its roles as a “super connector” and “super value-adder”, and pursue broader co-operation with Peru across various sectors to achieve mutual benefits and “win-win” outcomes.

Mr Lee then met Prime Minister and Minister for Finance of Singapore Lawrence Wong. Mr Lee remarked that both Hong Kong and Singapore are externally oriented international financial and trade centres that enjoy frequent economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges, as well as close co-operation.

Highlighting that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is accelerating the development of the Northern Metropolis and the Hong Kong Park area of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone, Mr Lee encouraged Singaporean enterprises with strengths in innovation and technology to establish a presence in the Northern Metropolis and tap into the Mainland market by leveraging Hong Kong’s advantages in bringing together global talent and frontier research.

Mr Lee also thanked Singapore for its continued support for Hong Kong’s early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, and expressed the hope that, with Singapore assuming the Association of Southeast Asian Nations chairmanship next year, the two sides will continue to deepen collaboration and jointly promote regional economic development.

articles.fullText:
The Buildings Department approved 16 building plans in September – three on Hong Kong Island and 13 in the New Territories.

Of the approved plans, four were for apartment or apartment/commercial developments, three were for commercial development, seven for factory and industrial developments, and two for community services.

Consent was given for works on four building projects. Upon completion, they will provide 133,494 sq m of gross floor area for domestic purposes, equating to 2,516 units, and 159,085 sq m of gross floor area for non-domestic use.

Additionally, the department received notification of the commencement of superstructure works for five building projects.

It also issued 21 occupation permits, comprising five on Hong Kong Island, eight in Kowloon and eight in the New Territories.

The buildings certified for occupation comprise 30,470 sq m of gross floor area for domestic purposes, equating to 655 units, and 100,899 sq m for non-domestic use.

Meanwhile, the department also issued three demolition consents and 771 removal orders, and received 3,540 reports about unauthorised building works in September.

articles.title: CE hails 5 APEC Summit outcomes
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee said today that Hong Kong achieved five major outcomes during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee said today that Hong Kong achieved five major outcomes during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit held in Shenzhen, ranging from strengthened ties with Southeast Asian nations to new agreements with emerging markets.

Speaking to the media this afternoon, Mr Lee emphasised Hong Kong's active role in supporting China's hosting of the regional forum.

“First, contributing Hong Kong's strength by actively participating in and supporting our country's successful hosting of the APEC meeting," said Mr Lee, noting that the city organised meetings and workshops while launching a series of capacity-building projects throughout the event.

During the summit, Mr Lee focused on bilateral diplomacy to deepen exchanges with fellow APEC economies and consolidate ties with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

“I met with the leaders of seven economies – Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand, Chile, Peru and Singapore – to strengthen ties and discuss issues of mutual concern,” he said. “The APEC meetings provided me with the opportunity to meet with five ASEAN leaders at bilateral meetings and engagements to further consolidate our relations.”

In a move to expand the city's reach into emerging markets, Mr Lee pointed to a new bilateral milestone reached on Wednesday.

"Yesterday, the President of Chile and I jointly witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme Agreement between Hong Kong and Chile," he said.

Rounding out the achievements, Mr Lee highlighted his efforts at Tuesday’s CEO Summit to promote the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) and showcase Hong Kong’s unique advantages to international business and political leaders.

The Chief Executive added that Hong Kong has been making efforts to deepen the city's integration into national development.

“I think we can deepen Greater Bay Area development through hard, soft and heart connectivity and take forward the Northern Metropolis for integrating into national development. Second, we can contribute to Belt & Road co-operation.

“Third, we can, through the Go Global Task Force, support many enterprises in leveraging Hong Kong's world-class professional services and extensive global network, in using Hong Kong as a springboard to expand into global markets.”

articles.title: 20th ICT Awards honours winners
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan today presented the Award of the Year at the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 ceremony to…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today presented the Award of the Year at the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 ceremony to a joint team of government departments and local organisations.

The winning team comprises the Electrical & Mechanical Services Department, the Architectural Services Department, the Housing Department, the Hong Kong Center for Construction Robotics Limited and the Hong Kong Housing Society, which also won the Smart Business Grand Award for its AI-enabled Smart Water Tank Cleaning Robot.

Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong presented trophies to the eight winners of Grand Awards at the ceremony to recognise their outstanding performance.

Addressing the ceremony, Mr Chan said: “Look back at the winners over the years and you can see how much has changed. The technology has changed. But the winners have something in common: they saw what people needed and found a new way to help.”

Mr Chan noted that some of the most important applications of artificial intelligence (AI) may still lie ahead. “AI can help us do familiar things better. The more interesting question is: what may it allow us to do differently? Many of the winners tonight are pointing the way. They show us not just what AI can do, but what it makes possible for people,” he said.

He added that the Government’s role is to give innovators the conditions to succeed, noting that the Committee on AI+ & Industry Development Strategy is helping more industries put AI to work. Mr Chan also highlighted that the data facility cluster being built at Sandy Ridge will expand Hong Kong’s computing capacity, while the Hong Kong AI Research & Development Institute will help turn research breakthroughs into practical applications.

In addition, the Government is training specialists and rolling out its AI for All programme to help people across the community use AI with confidence.

Established in 2006 and celebrating its 20th anniversary this year, the annual Hong Kong ICT Awards have tracked the innovation and growth of the city’s tech sector. The awards continue to honour outstanding enterprises and talent in ICT innovation, encouraging the industry to pursue excellence.

The Education Bureau announced today that the Study Subsidy Scheme for Designated Professions/Sectors will subsidise 2,196 places in 35 sub-degree programmes at five post-secondary institutions for the 2027/28 academic year.

The programmes span seven disciplines facing strong manpower demand: architecture and engineering, computer science, creative industries, healthcare, sports and recreation, testing and certification, and tourism and hospitality.

Annual subsidies for the 2027/28 academic year will be $40,730 for laboratory-based programmes and $23,390 for non-laboratory-based programmes.

The subsidy applies to both new and continuing eligible students and covers the normal duration of the programmes.

Students in need may still apply for assistance from the Student Finance Office under the Working Family & Student Financial Assistance Agency to help cover the remaining tuition fees payable.
