articles.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
articles.excerpt: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new…
articles.fullText:
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.

Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River . And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.

Two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. The Hoover Dam power plant requires 950 feet in Lake Mead, and that reservoir was 9% above the minimum in September.

Together, the two plants produced nearly seven terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, enough to serve over 2 million people.

Low water levels have been an ongoing struggle for the region, which has been in a drought for 27 years. Meanwhile, climate change is continuing to shift rainfall and snowfall patterns across the region and around the world.

The effects of climate change on hydropower aren’t entirely straightforward globally—some regions will see more rain and snow because of shifting weather patterns, while others are likely to see less.

But it’s playing a role for hydropower availability, according to one 2022 review study . Rising temperatures bring more droughts, warmer winters means less snow and ice to fill the reservoirs, and more variability in precipitation can lead to alternating floods and droughts, making the power source less reliable.

Hydropower production is likely to be at its lowest level in over a decade in 2026 and tick even lower in 2027, according to projections from the EIA.

El Niño could provide some temporary relief. Sometimes this weather pattern can mean cooler, wetter conditions for the southern US. Heavy rains brought floods to the region in October and early November, and the water levels in Lake Powell rose more than 20 feet from their mid-September low. But the water is still quite low, and it’ll take much more to help reservoirs recover from decades of drought conditions.

Even as a changing climate complicates the availability of hydropower, the decline in capacity could push greenhouse-gas emissions higher. In 2023, energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions rose by 1.1% globally. A worldwide shortfall in hydropower generation accounted for about 40% of that rise, according to a report from the International Energy Agency.

articles.title: Working Holiday Scheme signed
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth. Secretary…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth.

Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Chile Francisco Pérez Mackenna signed the agreement on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. Chief Executive John Lee and President of Chile José Antonio Kast witnessed the signing.

Welcoming the agreement, Mr Sun said: “Chile is Hong Kong’s first WHS partner in Latin America. The scheme will provide young people from Hong Kong and Chile with opportunities to broaden their horizons and gain first-hand experience of living and working in a different cultural environment.”

Mr Pérez Mackenna said: “We are pleased to provide young people from Chile and Hong Kong with new opportunities to experience life in each other’s communities. Hong Kong’s unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, international outlook and dynamic economy will offer Chilean youth an enriching experience. We also look forward to welcoming young people from Hong Kong to discover Chile’s rich culture, warm hospitality and natural beauty, thereby strengthening mutual understanding and people-to-people ties.”

Under the agreement, successful applicants can stay for up to 12 months in either Hong Kong or Chile. Participants may take up employment to finance their stay or enrol in short-term courses, subject to an annual quota of 100 places for each side.

This marks the 15th Working Holiday Scheme Hong Kong has established since 2001. Similar arrangements are already in place with New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Germany, Japan, Canada, Korea, France, the United Kingdom, Austria, Hungary, Sweden, the Netherlands and Italy.

Over 109,000 Hong Kong youths have benefited from these schemes to date. Details on visa application procedures will soon be available on the websites of the Immigration Department and Chile’s National Migration Service .

articles.title: Stepping up maritime hub push
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan has outlined how Hong Kong is upgrading and transforming its shipping industry to…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan has outlined how Hong Kong is upgrading and transforming its shipping industry to build a global maritime hub, aligning the city’s First Five-Year Plan with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Highlighting Hong Kong’s role as the strategic southern gateway linking the Mainland with the world, she noted that the city serves as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder".

To consolidate and enhance Hong Kong’s status as an international shipping centre, the Government is adopting a dual-core strategy that boosts port competitiveness while fostering a vibrant, high-value maritime services cluster. Ms Chan expected that these efforts will strengthen the city’s resilience and attract fresh business opportunities for the sector.

"They can finance, they can build and also lead from Hong Kong as the base, to enter into a more rigorous and more complete holistic development of maritime and shipping development for Hong Kong," she said.

One of the key measures to enhance port competitiveness is the green transformation of the maritime industry. Hong Kong is the seventh-largest bunkering hub globally by volume, having completed over 210 green maritime fuel bunkering operations totalling more than 370,000 tonnes from January 2025 through the third quarter of 2026.

Ms Chan noted that Hong Kong holds strong potential to become a leading Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering & Trade Centre. To advance this goal, the Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Zhanjiang in Guangdong to jointly establish Hong Kong’s very first Green Energy Corridor.

Ms Chan added that the Government will collaborate with relevant parties to develop national and international standards and certification systems for green shipping fuel. It will also leverage Hong Kong’s mature capital-raising platform to finance investments in green fuel shipping.

articles.title: APEC CEO Summit opens
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today and…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today and met leaders of other economies during the day.

President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony, pointing out that APEC was born amid the waves of economic globalisation and enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of the times. Noting that this year marks the third time China has hosted APEC, he said that China is ready to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all in the region.

President Xi put forward four proposals: to uphold peace and stability, to build bridges of opening up and co-operation, to boost innovation to drive growth and to expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. He also said China supports establishing a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges among bay areas worldwide and explore new ways for stronger regional economic co-operation.

Mr Lee said he was deeply encouraged and inspired by President Xi's keynote speech, noting that from a strategic and long-term perspective, it charted the course for Asia-Pacific co-operation. He added that the speech underscored the need to firmly uphold the post-war international order, resolve differences through dialogue and negotiation and respond to challenges through solidarity and collaboration to lay a solid foundation for long-term regional peace and stability.

The Chief Executive highlighted that as an APEC member economy, Hong Kong has long served as an important hub for regional economic and trade co-operation and is one of the world's most competitive economies. He noted that Hong Kong has consistently supported free trade and multilateralism, actively leveraging the APEC platform to continuously deepen international exchanges and co-operation.

Afterwards, Mr Lee met Malaysia's Prime Minister Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim and noted that the official opening of the Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur is deepening ties and investment promotion with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and neighbouring Asian countries. Highlighting Hong Kong's development as an international hub for high-calibre talent and a Muslim-friendly destination, Mr Lee welcomed more Malaysian students and visitors to Hong Kong.

Mr Lee then met Vietnam's President To Lam, noting that the two places share a vision for promoting high-quality development. He encouraged Vietnamese enterprises to leverage Hong Kong's advantages in connecting the Mainland and the world, using the city as a springboard to tap into the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and seize more opportunities together.

In the afternoon, Mr Lee met Brunei's Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah. Mr Lee said that Hong Kong's world-class capital markets, professional services and aviation and logistics network can strongly support deeper co-operation, expressing hope that both sides will further strengthen collaboration and complement each other's strengths.

In addition, Mr Lee met Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, noting that Thailand is developing its innovation and technology industries while Hong Kong is advancing the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He expressed hope that the two places would strengthen connectivity and co-operation in innovation and technology, encouraging more Thai enterprises to establish a presence in Hong Kong to expand into international markets.

Mr Lee then met Chile's President José Antonio Kast and witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme agreement between Hong Kong and Chile. Mr Lee said Hong Kong will continue to leverage its roles as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder" to strengthen bilateral co-operation in different areas.

Mr Lee thanked the leaders of Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei and Thailand for their continued support for Hong Kong's early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and the joint promotion of regional economic development. He added that amid a complex and ever-changing international landscape, Hong Kong is actively expanding into diversified markets and deepening collaboration with ASEAN, Latin America and other countries of the Global South.

In the evening, Mr Lee was due to attend a welcome banquet for leaders and representatives of the participating economies. Tomorrow, he will attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and hold bilateral talks with other regional leaders.

articles.title: HK, Vietnam sign co-operation pact
articles.excerpt: The Department of Justice (DOJ) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today signed a Memorandum of Co-operation (MOC)…
articles.fullText:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today signed a Memorandum of Co-operation (MOC) with Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to strengthen co-operation on building capacity for the prevention and settlement of international disputes.

Signed by Secretary for Justice Paul Lam and Vietnam's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Le Anh Tuan, the pact provides a framework for Hong Kong and Vietnam to collaborate on building the capacity of legal officers with respect to international disputes in the economic, commercial and investment fields.

It is expected that the two places will benefit greatly from their enhanced co-operation under the pact.

The DOJ said the MOC's signing will further consolidate Hong Kong's status as a centre for international legal and dispute resolution services, and help to strengthen its capacity with regard to international law.

It added that it will continue to pursue co-operation or partnership arrangements with other jurisdictions and international organisations.

articles.title: Four lamp models banned
articles.excerpt: The Electrical & Mechanical Services Department today announced a ban on the supply of four compact fluorescent lamp models that…
articles.fullText:
The Electrical & Mechanical Services Department today announced a ban on the supply of four compact fluorescent lamp models that failed to reach its energy efficiency and/or performance specifications.

Imported by Beauty Shadow Co Ltd, the four products are sold under the Sunshine brand with the following model numbers: S-24A 23W B22 2700K, S-24A 23W E27 2700K, S-16A 12W E14 6400K, S-16A 12W E27 6400K.

The department has removed the lamps from the record of listed models under the Energy Efficiency (Labelling of Products) Ordinance. Supplying such products is no longer allowed in Hong Kong, with immediate effect.

Notices have been served to the importer, which will publish newspaper notices announcing supply of the products has been terminated.

articles.title: Green fuel platform to be developed
articles.excerpt: The Transport & Logistics Bureau today announced the establishment of the “Task Group on the Development of the Green Maritime…
articles.fullText:
The Transport & Logistics Bureau today announced the establishment of the “Task Group on the Development of the Green Maritime Fuel Trading Platform”, a collaboration with industry to advance Hong Kong’s development as a globally oriented, diverse and open green maritime fuel trading centre.

The bureau said that as an international maritime, financial and trading centre, Hong Hong has the unique advantage of being backed by China and enjoying global connectivity, adding that its financial and legal systems are aligned with international practices.

It added: “Coupled with the upcoming implementation of the half-rate tax concession for physical trading of eligible commodities, which include green fuels, Hong Kong is well-positioned to establish a market-driven, globally oriented green fuel trading centre, providing a platform that brings together green fuel supplies from the Chinese Mainland and around the world and connects them with demand from the global maritime industry.”

Bringing together energy traders, green fuel producers, think tanks, and maritime and energy organisations, to advise on the platform’s development, the task group will explore the establishment of a green fuel price index, based on actual transaction data, to provide reliable pricing references for the industry.

It will also advise on building a complete industry chain to support green fuel trading, with a view to attracting more stakeholders from the Chinese Mainland and overseas to trade green fuels in Hong Kong.

Founding members of the task group include the Hydrogen Energy Industry Promotion Association, CIMC Enric Holdings Limited, Hong Kong and China Gas Company Limited, TGT Group Limited, the International Green Fuels Alliance, Our Hong Kong Foundation and AEX Holdings, Ltd.

To drive the establishment of the trading platform, the bureau signed Memoranda of Understanding with multiple partners during Hong Kong Maritime Week. These covered platform development, price index development, solicitation of platform users and industry research.

articles.title: Mexican leader asks China for panda
articles.excerpt: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that she asked President Xi Jinping for a panda for her country during…
articles.fullText:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday that she asked President Xi Jinping for a panda for her country during a meeting in China.

"Next year marks the 55th anniversary of Mexico-China relations, and it's a very important milestone," Sheinbaum told reporters in Shenzhen.

"We discussed moving forward on tourism, and we also asked for a panda for the Chapultepec Zoo as part of this partnership," she said on the sidelines of the Apec summit.

"So it was a very good meeting – a very cordial and very frank one."

Chapultepec Zoo in Mexico City is home to the only known giant panda not owned by China, a 36-year-old female called Xin Xin.

It is the last in a line of giant pandas brought to Mexico in 1975.

Since the 1980s, China has operated a different policy in which it lends pandas for set periods and in return for a payment towards wild panda conservation efforts.

Sheinbaum also told Xi that relations with China are entering a "new era", while Xi called for ties to be elevated to a "a higher level" in light of a "complex" global situation.

Xi met various regional leaders on the Apec sidelines on Tuesday, among them Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: Jensen Huang’s open-source dilemma and cognitive immortality
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back

A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has attracted more than 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk, but comb through the names, and you’ll notice a significant number come from a particular slice of the tech world: open-source AI.

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for open source, but his credibility as an advocate is now under threat. Revelations about Nvidia chips in China and a new rule in the US could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress

Read the full story to find out why .

—James O’Donnell

This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday.

Roundtables: inside the quest for cognitive immortality

The quest to overcome the human brain’s limits is moving beyond science fiction. From gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud, researchers and technologists are exploring radical ways to extend human cognition. Today, MIT Technology Review examines these ideas in a live Roundtables discussion.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado to explore what cognitive immortality could look like, and how close we might be to achieving it.

Tune in live today, Tuesday, November 17, at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

Want to join the conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our Roundtables.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 The US is tightening controls on China’s remote access to AI chips
It’s closed a loophole that let Chinese firms access US chips abroad. ( AP )
+  Xi may retaliate ahead of this week’s summit with Trump. ( Bloomberg $)
+ Nvidia is warning customers against renting chips to China. ( CNBC )
+ China is expanding AI distillation to work around curbs. ( Reuters $)
+ Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 US hyperscale data centers are emitting as much CO2 as Denmark
A new study found emissions tripled between 2018 and 2025. ( Verge )
+ 400 data centers use more electricity than Michigan. ( Wired $)
+ Nations want to harness AI to cut emissions. ( Nature )
+ But AI models can quickly become climate crisis deniers. ( Guardian )

3 California has sued OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
The attorney general said the company failed to protect the public. ( FT $)
+ And that it admitted to 80 cases of losing control of models. ( CNBC )
+ Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue? ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The Supreme Court has rejected Trump’s bid to cut research grants
Lower courts found the moves likely violated free speech rights. ( CBS )
+ Trump has dealt heavy blows to US science. ( MIT Technology Review )

5 Widespread online outages have hit major US banks
Thousands of customers reported account access problems. ( Gizmodo )
+ A separate outage delayed United Airlines flights. ( Reuters $)

6 Alice Huang’s husband built a data-center empire in China
He won government backing as his wife pursued Nvidia chips. ( WSJ $)
+ MAGA is using the scandal to weaken Trump’s Big Tech ties. ( Axios )

7 China has sacked a scientist after a child died in a gene-editing trial
The girl died after receiving an experimental therapy in 2025. ( Nature )
+ Startups want new rules on gene-editing. ( MIT Technology Review )

8 America’s EV boom is happening without car buyers
Delivery fleets, robotaxis, and police cars are going electric. ( Atlantic $)

9 New cosmic data has challenged our model of the universe
The findings suggest dark energy may be weakening. ( Quanta )

10 A Buddhist sect plans to build an AI guru for Silicon Valley
It wants to create a model based on a collective mind. ( New Yorker $)

Quote of the day

“Export controls 2.0 is here.”

—Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, tells Reuters that Washington has opened a new front in its campaign to slow China’s AI ambitions.

One more thing

Welcome to Kenya’s Great Carbon Valley: a bold new gamble to fight climate change

Kenya’s Great Rift Valley is home to five geothermal power stations, which harness clouds of steam to generate about a quarter of the country’s electricity. But some of the energy escapes into the atmosphere, while even more remains underground for lack of demand. That’s what brought Octavia Carbon here.

Last year, the startup began harnessing some of that excess energy to remove CO2 from the air. The company says the method is efficient, affordable, and—crucially—scalable. But the project also faces fierce opposition.

Read the full story on the future of Kenya’s “Great Carbon Valley.”

—Diana Kruzman

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ A gorilla rescued as an orphan and rewilded has now had a baby of her own .
+ Kelowna, British Columbia, has elected a man who ran for city council as a joke.
+ A vast new data dump from the Euclid space telescope covers a stunning section of the sky and 900 million galaxies.
+ Scientists recreated the long-lost chirps of Jurassic insects to produce a soundscape from 165 million years ago.

articles.title: Airport closer to sustainable aviation fuel facility
articles.excerpt: The Airport Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday with Hong Kong and China Gas Company (Towngas) and EcoCeres…
articles.fullText:
The Airport Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday with Hong Kong and China Gas Company (Towngas) and EcoCeres to develop a sustainable aviation fuel blending facility in the city to support the aviation industry's transition towards a more sustainable future.

The signing was witnessed by Chief Executive John Lee during the Asian Logistics, Maritime and Aviation Conference.

Also present for the signing were Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan, Airport Authority chief executive Vivian Cheung and Towngas chairman Peter Lee.

The MoU was signed by Airport Authority chief operating officer Steven Yiu, Towngas executive director and chief investment officer Alan Chan and EcoCeres CEO Matti Lievonen.

Under the agreement, the three parties will continue discussions on the design, construction and operation of a blending facility in Tuen Mun, with implementation subject to terms to be agreed between them.

In Hong Kong's first five-year plan, the government aims to achieve a sustainable aviation fuel consumption target of between one and three percent for flights departing from the airport by 2030.

John Lee announced in his Policy Address this year that the government would take forward the construction of a blending facility to build an end-to-end sustainable aviation fuel value chain and reduce logistics costs to make prices for greener jet fuel products more competitive.

The government is also collaborating with mainland authorities on the establishment of a sustainable aviation fuel production base in Dongguan.

The airport's existing fuel infrastructure is already capable of receiving, storing and uplifting pre-blended sustainable aviation fuel by airlines, with one local airline having successfully uplifted the fuel.

Edited by Edmond Fong

RTHK and CGTN are joining hands in covering the Apec summit in Shenzhen.

RTHK's Hailey Yip and her CGTN counterpart Chen Tong have more on Tuesday's Apec CEO Summit and the day's other highlights.

articles.title: Greater Bay Area a proven model of cooperation: CE
articles.excerpt: The Greater Bay Area is a proven model of how complementary strengths can generate opportunities far greater than the sum…
articles.fullText:
The Greater Bay Area is a proven model of how complementary strengths can generate opportunities far greater than the sum of their parts, Chief Executive John Lee told the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday.

"Prosperity is not something we can each win separately. It is something we can only build together," he said, urging Asia-Pacific economies to explore partnerships that combine their innovation and market knowledge with the Greater Bay Area's manufacturing capacity, capital and consumer markets.

Lee said the turnout of over 2,000 business and government leaders, including some 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, at the summit sends a clear message that economies of the region need open and continuing cooperation more than ever.

He said the Greater Bay Area, home to more than 88 million people and generating a GDP exceeding US$2.1 trillion, would rank about 12th globally if it were a standalone economy.

Lee said that under "One Country, Two Systems", Hong Kong has an indispensable role to play, describing it as the natural "super-connector" and "super value-adder" between the Greater Bay Area and the rest of the Asia-Pacific.

He invited the Asia-Pacific community to use Hong Kong as a springboard and business centre from which to seize the region's opportunities.

"Hong Kong, China stands ready to connect people, capital, ideas and opportunities so that we may all prosper and win the future. And that future begins right here."

Lee also said the Greater Bay Area is committed to the smooth flow of people, goods, capital and data.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK urged to offer tax cut for small commodity traders
articles.excerpt: The vice president of Our Hong Kong Foundation, Kenny Shui, has called on authorities to introduce an entry-level tax concession…
articles.fullText:
The vice president of Our Hong Kong Foundation, Kenny Shui, has called on authorities to introduce an entry-level tax concession to attract small commodity traders in a bid to drive the development of maritime services in the city.

The trade in commodities is linked to the shipment of such goods, which is why related maritime services are vital to the sector.

Shui made the remarks as the think tank released a research report on Tuesday, suggesting the SAR should focus on higher value-added maritime and professional services.

Speaking at a press conference, Shui said the government's existing half-tax concession helped attract medium-sized traders with an annual turnover of no less than HK$700 million, but such a threshold has excluded smaller traders with high growth potential.

Shui proposed a two-tier tax mechanism aimed at assisting traders whose turnover has yet to reach the threshold.

Under the proposal, the half-tax concession would be extended to cover small traders with potential for five years.

If a trader's annual turnover still fails to reach the HK$700 million threshold in the five-year period, the concession would cease, he said.

"Our current challenge is that compared with other competitors like Singapore, we do not have a lot of commodity traders," Shui said.

"So that's why we want to use the tax to attract them. For medium-sized payers, the government has a plan to use the half-tax to attract those payers.

"But for the entry-level [traders], as we do not have a half-tax plan, we just have the normal 16.5 percent tax. So that's why we are asking whether we can also have a half-tax for those entry-level payers to attract them to come to Hong Kong."

The foundation also called for enhanced marine insurance, ship leasing and maritime arbitration services.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Tech fears continue to chip away at regional markets
articles.excerpt: Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis continued to rattle trading…
articles.fullText:
Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis continued to rattle trading floors, with US moves to tighten restrictions on Chinese access to chips adding to uncertainty.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 245 points, or one percent, lower at 23,508 on turnover of HK$198.05 billion.

The tech index fell 43 points, or 1.1 percent, to 3,758 while the China enterprises index was 77 points, or one percent, lower at 7,904.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index closed down 17 points, or 0.5 percent, at 3,584 on turnover of 690.5 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 52 points, or 0.49 percent, to 10,638 on turnover of 767.18 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index lost 27 points, or 1.2 percent, to close at 2,292 on turnover of 365.83 billion yuan.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended down 801 points, or 1.34 percent, at 58,860, with AI- and chip-related falls of 5.08 percent by Kioxia Holdings, 4.39 percent by Advantest and 3.95 percent by SoftBank Group contributing to the benchmark's losses.

The broader Topix slid 61 points, or 1.57 percent, to 3,840.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed 132 points, or 2.59 percent, lower at 4,968, down in a fourth consecutive session of losses, with chipmaking index heavyweights Samsung Electronics falling 3.3 percent and SK Hynix losing 1.96 percent.

The selloff comes as investors brace for the release of earnings from Wall Street titan Nvidia, which comes days after its boss Jensen Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs.

Also in focus is the initial public offering of Claude-creator Anthropic, which is being seen as a test of confidence in the AI trade, which has been whipsawed in recent months by concerns over companies' eye-watering AI investments and their profitability.

Markets have been battered since the crisis broke at Nvidia, which is at the centre of a build-out in artificial intelligence that has helped propel global markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the world.

Nvidia's earnings will be closely watched after the US market closes later Tuesday, or 8am on Wednesday Hong Kong time, with investors looking for signs of whether the AI boom can withstand the widening scandal.

Matt Weller at Forex.com said: "Data centre demand and guidance will be central.

"Investors will look for evidence that hyperscalers and other customers are sustaining their spending on AI infrastructure, and whether fourth-quarter guidance points to further growth."

Donald Trump on Monday backed calls from some of Silicon Valley's most powerful voices pushing for the swift return of Huang, with the US president downplaying national security concerns over allegations of possible spy links.

Adding to the downbeat mood was news that the US Commerce Department moved on Monday to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely.

A new rule will force data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to get a licence from the United States allowing them to ship high-end AI chips from Nvidia and other American firms to clients in those countries.

"The proposed rules are aimed at limiting the remote use or diversion of cutting-edge US chips and extend the regulatory overhang facing the semiconductor industry," said National Australia Bank's Rodrigo Catril.

"The news also raises questions about the outlook for global AI infrastructure investment, particularly in jurisdictions that have become important hubs for data centre development." (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Shenzhen firms go extra mile in Apec workarounds
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen companies have adopted flexible working arrangements during the ongoing Apec-linked meetings, with some staff taking annual leave, working from…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen companies have adopted flexible working arrangements during the ongoing Apec-linked meetings, with some staff taking annual leave, working from home or travelling off-peak.

Their flexibility came to light in an ongoing 100-hour all-media live broadcast titled "Apec China Year", which is being aired by Shenzhen Media Group in conjunction with Beijing Radio and Television and Shanghai Media Group to capture the host city's preparations for the summit and supporting events.

Yao Peitong of Harbin Institute of Technology Pengze, Shenzhen, a robotics company, said it was only following government advice by having only four of its 15-strong workforce back in the office.

Meituan, for its part, has introduced 10 measures from Monday to Friday to ease pressure on delivery riders.

Yuan Min, a rider protection manager, said late deliveries across Shenzhen would not be penalised.

Meituan's Shenzhen head, Niu Dexu, said the company's app had, together with the authorities, also launched a Chinese-English food map to facilitate visitors seeking to sample the city's varied fare.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Tech leaders say EV innovation, robotaxis key for Apec
articles.excerpt: The founder of the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker on Tuesday said opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region outweigh challenges…
articles.fullText:
The founder of the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker on Tuesday said opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region outweigh challenges and that innovation is the key to unlocking them.

Speaking at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen, Robin Zeng of Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL) said a company's first goal is to make money, but that its purpose as it grows should be to benefit people.

He said this is what motivates him to persist, adding that CATL is focused on innovation and on sharing the benefits of advances made across the region.

"We really focus on innovations," Zeng said.

"So if you have technology innovation, product innovation, solution innovation, then they can come up with a solution to share in this region.

"For example, everyone now is focused on the EV.

"We are more focused on the infrastructure of the EV, so battery swapping is one of the innovations, which can help all the EV cars swap the batteries in 99 seconds. So it's very fast.

"This can already be applied to this region. This is we're talking about a business model innovation."

Speaking at the same panel discussion, Baidu chief executive Robin Li highlighted driverless ride-hailing vehicles as a prime example of artificial intelligence's real-world potential.

"It's a real application, and people can really benefit from that," he said.

"It benefits people's daily lives. Every year, more than a million people get killed on the roads.

"But when robotaxi is operating, its safety record is about 10 times better than that of a human driver."

Li said that with China and the United States gradually opening the way for for autonomous vehicles, he hoped other places in Asia would follow suit.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apec CEO Summit attendance over 2,000, says chair
articles.excerpt: More than 2,000 chief executives and representatives will attend the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday and Wednesday, summit…
articles.fullText:
More than 2,000 chief executives and representatives will attend the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Tuesday and Wednesday, summit chairman Ren Hongbin said.

He said discussions on the first day of the event would cover seven topics, among which are artificial intelligence, sustainable development, digital economy and development opportunities for the Greater Bay Area and the Asia-Pacific region.

“For a long time, the business community has actively supported, participated in and promoted the cooperation and development in the Asia-Pacific region,” Ren said.

“By pushing major development, prosperity and connectivity in the region, it has made Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region in the global economy and a primary engine for growth.”

Ren, also chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, said President Xi Jinping would attend the summit’s opening ceremony on Wednesday and deliver a speech.

Another 11 leaders of Apec economies would also attend the summit, he added.

Ren expressed hope that summit participants could achieve consensus and cooperation during discussions.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Alcaraz sweeps aside Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the first time by cruising past Frances Tiafoe in straight sets, 6-2, 6-2.

World number three Alcaraz took just over an hour to deal with American Tiafoe and show why he is the favourite to win the whole thing in Turin, where he was the beaten finalist last year.

Since returning in August from a wrist injury that kept him off the tour for four months, Alcaraz has won three of the five tournaments he has entered, most recently the Paris Masters.

Alcaraz, 25, can book his place in the semi-finals on Wednesday by beating Italian Flavio Cobolli, who in the absence of former world number one Jannik Sinner is the crowd favourite.

"Sometimes I feel really comfortable," Alcaraz said.

"I feel like I'm better than the opponent in every aspect of the game.

"If I qualify to the semi-final or not, I think it's a great experience, a great week, getting experience," he added.

Tiafoe had a nightmare debut match at the season-ending tournament, the 28-year-old having no answer to Alcaraz's speed and power.

Only briefly in the second set did he look like challenging his opponent, a seven-time Grand Slam winner, when at 3-2 down he wasted three opportunities to break back. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Palace appoint Thomas Frank as manager
articles.excerpt: Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the…
articles.fullText:
Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the struggling club off the bottom of the Premier League table.

The former Brentford and Tottenham boss succeeds Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman was unable to build on the legacy of his predecessor Oliver Glasner, who oversaw the most successful period in the club's history.

Glasner led the south London club to their first-ever major trophy, beating Manchester City to win the FA Cup in 2025, and won the Uefa Conference League last season.

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it," Frank said in a Palace statement.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Frank, who has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal, enjoyed great success during seven years at Brentford, leading the Bees into the top flight for the first time in 74 years in 2021 and establishing the club in the Premier League.

His work in west London earned the 53-year-old a move to Tottenham in June 2025 but he lasted just eight months as Spurs struggled.

Palace hope Frank can rekindle the highs of his time at Brentford with similar resources at Selhurst Park.

"I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace," said Palace chairman Steve Parish. "He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club."

Sage paid the price after four straight league defeats left Palace at the bottom of the table.

He was hindered by the departures of Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Daniel Munoz, who reunited with Glasner at Nottingham Forest.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, shipping 24 goals in 10 matches.

They will be hoping for an instant improvement as they prepare to face relegation rivals Coventry and Hull in their next two league games.

They also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League table with four games of the league phase remaining. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Germany run riot over Netherlands in Nations League
articles.excerpt: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win…
articles.fullText:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach.

It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959.

"The game was outstanding," Klopp told German broadcaster ARD. "We scored unbelievable goals. It was just insane. A fantastic football match and a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have even dared to wish for all of this."

Klopp singled out Gruda and Scherhant, two players he has given their debuts, for special praise.

"Boy can those two play. But the amount of work they put in, it's immense. That's what defines a team, and plenty of others can play football too."

So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany.

"We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told ARD.

The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group.

The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will.

"I'm really sad, because before the game I was really proud," Xavi told reporters.

"Today it was not about the football, but about speed and about (our) values."

"I want to say sorry to our supporters, because today we showed our worst face. It's part of the process... We need to keep going and work on our values."

Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final."

The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward.

The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away.

Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post.

Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post.

"I don't think it could have gone any better, to score the opener here in my city. I don't think I could have dreamed of better. It's unbelievable," Scherhant said.

The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc.

Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone.

RB Leipzig winger Gruda laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar.

In his first Germany match on home soil and just his second overall, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post.

"We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz.

"We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Uefa backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino
articles.excerpt: European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against…
articles.fullText:
European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's Fifa presidential election, it said in a statement on Monday.

The body said that Diallo had been "invited...to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027" and that European national associations had "unanimously pledged their full support."

The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is this Wednesday, November 18.

Uefa, which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo "has accepted the invitation to stand" and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French federation (FFF) on Tuesday.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, Uefa has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but Uefa has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of "criminal mismanagement" against the Fifa president in Switzerland.

Uefa had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani had been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean.

The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.

Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election.

"We believe that the trust placed in the Fifa president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," he said at the time.

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.

Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France's Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.

Infantino, a former Uefa secretary general, has been in charge of Fifa since 2016. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Villagers in northern Laos are afraid to use river water after rare-earth pond spill
articles.excerpt: Government and Chinese-financed mining company say water is safe, but residents are skeptical after animal deaths.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Lao .
After ponds at a Chinese-financed rare-earth mining operation burst and potentially contaminated two rivers in northern Laos, villagers living downstream told Radio Free Asia they don’t think the water is safe.
Villagers in northern Laos fear using river water after drainage ponds at a Chinese-financed rare earth mine burst upstream from their communities.
On Nov. 1, several drainage ponds began to overflow at the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Ltd. in Houaphanh province’s Xam Neua district. The water from the ponds drained into the Nam Vaen River, which flows into the Nam Xam River, which crosses the border into Vietnam.
There are approximately 18 affected villages that rely on the two rivers for agriculture, and this is the third rare-earth spill in the area after similar incidents in February 2024 and April 2026.
Authorities began an investigation on Nov. 4, consulting with officials from the mining company, who assured the government that the water was safe. But as early as Nov. 6, residents living downstream from the mining operation reported that fish were dying. Later, reports surfaced that birds and livestock like cows and pigs had also died. Authorities suspended mining indefinitely on Nov. 13.
A dead cow lies in the waters of the Nam Xam river in Houaphanh province, Laos, Nov. 13, 2026.
(Samakhom Khet 4) The local government should have visited the affected villages instead of just talking to the company, a resident of Muang Vaen village told RFA on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“They say there is no contamination, telling the people to be confident that nothing is wrong, but right now, fish are dying in massive numbers,” the villager said. “They didn’t go inspect the downstream area where the incident happened – they didn’t come at all. They went to the site up at the top, listening to them, listening to the company at the project site saying ‘nothing is wrong, this and that.’ They’re just trying to keep people from panicking.”
During the investigation, the mining company told the government that the pond that burst was a natural water storage pond, not a chemical waste storage pond. The company stated it has repaired the water pipes and will compensate damages to two families whose rice fields were damaged, in accordance with the law.
The villager said the people still do not dare consume the water or even use it for household chores, despite the assurances from the provincial government that there is no issue and they can use the water as usual.
A map showing the location of the spill in Houaphanh Province, Laos.
(RFA) Shortly after the incident, an official of the Houaphanh Provincial Department of Agriculture and Environment told RFA that residents living downstream should temporarily stop using the water until inspection results are available and the problem is resolved.
Later, on Nov. 15, another official of the same department told RFA that authorities are currently investigating why the animals are dying.
“Right now, they have fixed it,” the second official said. “Currently, agricultural production can proceed, and the water can be used normally. As for the dead fish and other dead animals, they are still analyzing it.”
Foreign-invested farming, mining and development projects in Laos have sparked friction over cases of environmental pollution and land often taken without proper compensation, leaving villagers fearing retaliation if they speak out.
Skeptical residents
Residents have raised questions and demanded that relevant authorities conduct a serious investigation following state media reports clarifying that there was no chemical contamination of the water.
They also told RFA that they do not trust the Nov. 4 investigation, after which authorities announced that they found no severe impact and no dead aquatic animals, though there was still an issue with water concentration that might be caused by saltwater seepage from an old mining pit. The authorities at that time said they were waiting for official confirmation test results from the National Water Quality Research Institute.
But some of the residents have turned to mountain spring water, which is more difficult to collect, and is insufficient for their livelihoods, they told RFA. They do not trust the government because a similar incident occurred at the same mining operation in 2024. At that time the villagers tested the water themselves and found it was contaminated.
The rare earth mine developed by the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Limited in Xam Neua district, Houaphanh province, Laos, is seen Feb. 27, 2024.
(Airbus) “Many villages are indirectly affected, so to speak – all 18 or 19 villages here,” a second villager told RFA on condition of anonymity to speak freely. “We cannot use the main river, the Nam Vaen.”
The villagers are demanding that authorities help them find replacement water to use for watering vegetables and agricultural production.
“Right now, for drinking and living water, it’s just mountain spring water and tiny streams, which isn’t enough to water vegetables and other crops,” the second villager said. “We are facing many hardships. They came to inspect and said nothing was wrong, yet we see so many dead fish there. Just like the previous time—when we took the water to get tested and we found contamination. When they took it to get tested, they didn’t find anything.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Unemployment rate drops to 3.8%
articles.excerpt: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the…
articles.fullText:
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the period from August to October, the Census & Statistics Department announced today.

The underemployment rate remained at 2%.

Total employment was 3,653,800, down 1,200 from the previous three-month period, while the labour force dropped by around 5,800 to 3,804,200.

Looking ahead, Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun said that the ongoing expansion of the local economy, solid consumption sentiment and continued growth in inbound tourism should render support to the overall labour market conditions.

“The Government will continue to closely monitor the evolving external uncertainties for their potential implications on corporate hiring sentiments and provide job-seekers with appropriate support," Mr Sun said.

articles.title: Plans ready for Subsector elections
articles.excerpt: Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) David Lok chaired a Crisis Management Committee (CMC) meeting this evening to review…
articles.fullText:
Chairman of the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) David Lok chaired a Crisis Management Committee (CMC) meeting this evening to review various scenarios that may arise during the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections, scheduled for November 22.

During the meeting, the EAC received briefings from representatives of key government departments, including the Registration & Electoral Office, the Digital Policy Office and the Hong Kong Police Force. They covered election preparation and co-ordination work, assessments of cybersecurity and security risks as well as contingency plans for polling day.

Further updates on preparatory work and co-ordination were presented by the Security Bureau, the Home Affairs Department, the Information Services Department, the Department of Justice and the Electrical & Mechanical Services Department.

Mr Lok noted that organising an election is a complex undertaking requiring meticulous planning, preparation and arrangements throughout the workflow. He added that relevant policy bureaux and departments have entered the final stage of preparation with security and contingency plans in place to ensure the elections proceed smoothly.

He also pointed out that today’s meeting enabled the EAC to prepare for the elections more thoroughly. The CMC will assist the EAC in closely monitoring conditions on polling day, reaffirming the EAC’s commitment to ensuring the elections are conducted openly, honestly and fairly in strict accordance with electoral laws and guidelines.

Five ordinary polling stations will be set up for the elections, utilising the electronic poll register (EPR) system to issue ballot papers.

Mr Lok and EAC member Daniel Shek also inspected an on-site drill arranged by the Registration & Electoral Office today for polling station staff. The training session familiarises staff with polling station operations and the ballot-paper issuance process, including using the EPR system and its fallback mode.

articles.title: Lawmaker supports decision to cut short harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to…
articles.fullText:
Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to call off the last race on safety grounds.

About 4,000 swimmers signed up to this year's annual race from Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui.

Cheng said safety was the top priority and the conditions at the time posed a certain risk and the last-minute cancellation was a responsible decision of the organiser.

He said the currents were very strong during the final 300 metres to the finish, describing the situation as somewhat dangerous and chaotic.

"Normally a usual swim is probably maybe about 45 minutes, half an hour, but yesterday I swam for one hour 20 minutes, and I was still at the Avenue of Stars there, so there is also a certain risk there," Cheng told an RTHK programme on Monday.

He suggested that organisers should give participants earlier psychological preparation if they know the currents are strong, and consider extending the overall race time next time.

He also proposed refunding registration fees to those affected or giving them the opportunity to rejoin next year, as well as reviewing the race procedures and arrangements for better forecasting.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Scotland fend off late fightback to beat Wallabies
articles.excerpt: Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies…
articles.fullText:
Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies suffered a fourth successive defeat.

The Dark Blues led 12-5 at half-time thanks to two tries from Matt Fagerson and Australia-born Jack Dempsey to one from Wallaby wing Harry Potter.

Neither side managed another point until fly-half Finn Russell's penalty six minutes from time put Scotland 10 points ahead.

But Max Jorgensen's 79th-minute try, converted by Ben Donaldson, gave the Wallabies hope of an improbable win before the recalled Scotland duo of Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn frustrated a last-ditch Australia attack.

Victory saw Scotland leapfrog Wales into fourth place in the Northern Hemisphere table.

Both teams arrived at Murrayfield with concerns over their defence.

Scotland lost 43-21 at home to New Zealand in their November opener last week, while the Wallabies went down 45-22 to England at Twickenham — the third match in a row where Australia had given up at least 40 points.

Scotland suffered a setback shortly before kick-off when captain Sione Tuipulotu pulled out because of a knee injury, with Tom Jordan taking the Australia-born centre's place in midfield.

Nevertheless, it took Scotland just eight minutes to open the scoring.

From a close-range scrum, the ball was worked to the onrushing Jordan and he found Ben White, with the scrum-half's pass releasing unguarded flanker Fagerson, who dived over out wide for his sixth Test try.

Finn Russell's conversion hit the post and just three minutes later Australia were level.

Scotland's defence was split apart as a delayed pass from recalled fly-half Carter Gordon and a missed tackle from Russell allowed Potter to slide over at a rainswept Murrayfield for a try Ryan Lonergan could not convert.

Scotland thought they had a second try when Kyle Steyn volleyed a bouncing ball forward from a grubber kick, with Darcy Graham touching down.

But the score was disallowed on review after Steyn was ruled to have been in touch.

But their second try did arrive in the 27th minute when back-row forward Dempsey — who won 14 caps for the Wallabies before changing allegiance in 2022— barged over with Russell adding the extras.

Australia then also had a try disallowed on review, with Billy Pollard's score from a driving maul ruled out for obstruction to leave Scotland 12-5 ahead at the break.

Pollard was yellow carded in the 46th minute for a head-on-head collision with Kinghorn but the Scots were unable to make the extra man count in a scrappy contest.

It was not until the 74th minute that Russell's penalty put Scotland two scores in front.

The Wallabies mounted a frantic rally which ended with Jorgensen speeding in for a try to give the hosts a scare before Scotland celebrated their fifth win in six Tests against Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.excerpt: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday…
articles.fullText:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.

Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California.

Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament.

She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut.

"It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva.

The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself."

A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2.

Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead.

There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up.

She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40.

A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5.

The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up.

The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies.

Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1.

Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead.

The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down.

A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40.

Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win.

Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance.

"After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: England topple world champions Spain in Nations League
articles.excerpt: England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own…
articles.fullText:
England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own patch, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to join France in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's team win Group A3, level on 15 points with Spain, after the hugely impressive win in Madrid in which La Roja were for long periods made to look a shadow of the team which won the World Cup.

But the Three Lions ended up down to 10 men and hanging on by their finger nails before inflicting on Spain a first defeat in a competitive fixture since March 2023.

Asked by ITV whether this was England's best performance of his reign as coach, Tuchel said: "Under the circumstances against who and where we played, yeah."

"(We showed) what we are made of and what we can do," added Tuchel, saying his team were motivated by their third place at the World Cup.

"We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years and we weren't happy with it. It's impressive what we did in the last two camps."

Harry Kane put the away side deservedly ahead on the stroke of half time, netting from the penalty spot, his record-extending 93rd England goal.

Ezri Konsa struck just after the break before Ben White gave England a barely-believable lead in the 57th minute when he latched onto Jude Bellingham's pass and finished between Unai Simon's legs.

England needed that cushion. Moments later they found themselves a man down when Elliot Anderson hauled backed Lamine Yamal in the box, conceding a penalty and a red card.

Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the spot-kick with Spain's first shot on target to set up a grandstand finish and bring back memories of England's collapse against Argentina which cost them a place in the World Cup final.

Those jitters intensified when Nico Williams slammed home Lamine Yamal's inch-perfect cross with 15 minutes remaining, but England just about held out under a Spanish onslaught.

Sitting third in Group A1 ahead of kick-off and needing a win to qualify for the last eight, Belgium had their backs up against the wall when Francesco Pio Esposito volleyed Italy ahead in the 11th minute.

But Belgium blew Italy away in the following quarter of an hour, with Maxim De Cuyper and Nathan Ngoy bundling the hosts ahead before Jeremy Doku slalomed through the Azzurri defence and confidently shot home.

Mark van Bommel's team deservedly claimed a spot in the quarters and made sure the scoreline reflected the balance of play when one of many attacks against an open Italy defence ended with Diego Moreira slotting home with 10 minutes remaining.

A dismal night for Italy, who were top of the group after beating France last time out and just needed a draw to go through, was made even worse when Senne Lammens saved Esposito's weak late penalty.

"Nights like this can happen, unfortunately. These things can happen during a rebuilding process," said Italy boss Roberto Mancini.

"We're disappointed, but this is the kind of night that will ultimately prove useful to us."

France top the group after bouncing back from defeat to Italy with a 2-1 win over rock-bottom Türkiye in Bordeaux.

Les Bleus will head into the draw for the last eight, scheduled for Friday in Nyon, Switzerland, as a seeded team, a position that ensures they will host the return leg in March 2027 but could mean they face Spain.

An Emirhan Topcu own goal just after half-time and Eli Junior Kroupi's first goal for France were enough for Zinedine Zidane's team to prevail and take top spot in the final round of of matches. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Mainland uni applications to open
articles.excerpt: Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply…
articles.fullText:
Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply online from December 1 to 31, the Education Bureau said today.

The number of Chinese Mainland institutions participating in the scheme will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year. Located in 21 provinces or municipalities and two autonomous regions, they will accept applications from candidates taking the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (HKDSE) Examination in 2027.

The Education Bureau encourages Hong Kong students to study on the Chinese Mainland via the scheme, thereby seizing opportunities to learn about the country’s social, economic and cultural landscape, and to bolster their own development.

The bureau said it will continue discussions to enable more renowned Mainland institutions to participate in the scheme, with a view to providing students with multiple higher education pathways and opportunities to connect with the country’s development.

Students should review their submitted application details online before January 10, 2027, while those providing supplementary information should do so before January 23. Students who pass the application verification process should pay the enrolment fee by January 31.

Institutions will announce admission results in late July next year. They may also arrange for supplementary enrolment depending on the enrolment situation.

articles.title: Australia down NZ to clinch Rugby League World Cup
articles.excerpt: Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World…
articles.fullText:
Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World Cup crown and reinforce their status as the sport's global powerhouse.

The home team took a 24-6 advantage into the break on a muggy evening at a sold-out Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane and never relented to inflict more pain on their arch-rivals.

Liam Martin and Jack Bostock bagged two tries each with Bradman Best and Tom Trbojevic also crossing in a fast and furious clash where Australia's fitness in draining conditions proved decisive.

The masterclass denied New Zealand their first title since 2008.

That upset – also in Brisbane – was the last time a team other than Australia lifted the silverware.

Since then the Kangaroos have won 23 games in a row at the tournament with Sunday's victory their 13th title from 17 World Cups played since its inception in 1954.

So dominant are they that they have lost just one of 20 Tests in the 2020s.

New Zealand performed an emotive haka, eager for revenge after going down 24-22 to Australia in an epic tournament opener over a month ago.

But they were immediately on the back foot, conceding after just 84 seconds.

Harry Grant threw a dummy and found big back-rower Martin who charged over with Cameron Munster adding the extras for a dream start.

After their shaky opening, the Kiwis knuckled down and after a sustained period of pressure centre Casey McLean stepped inside two Australian players to dot down and get them back in the contest.

Jamayne Isaako booted the conversion to move to 227 points, surpassing Shaun Johnson to become New Zealand's most prolific points scorer.

But Australia quickly restored order, with a beautiful offload from Best to Bostock in space who crossed in the corner.

Munster fluffed the conversion but made amends minutes later with a successful penalty to move Australia into a 12-6 lead.

The hosts were well on top and pierced a battered Kiwi defence again as Best finished under the posts before Martin collected his second just before the break with New Zealand tiring.

The second-half started where the first left off, with Australia's Trbojevic over after just four minutes, courtesy of Reece Walsh beating three defenders before the offload.

New Zealand were on the ropes with nothing going their way, including a try given by the referee then denied on review for a knock on.

But New Zealand persisted and Isaiah Papali'i split the defence for a converted try to leave them trailing 28-10 with 13 minutes remaining, only for Australia to hold firm with Bostock grabbing his second as the clock ticked down. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HZMB Half Marathon draws thousands of runners
articles.excerpt: Tens of thousands of runners – from professionals to enthusiastic amateurs – took part in the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Half…
articles.fullText:
Tens of thousands of runners – from professionals to enthusiastic amateurs – took part in the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge Half Marathon on Sunday morning.

The event featured three groups: the 10-kilometre challenge, along with the half-marathon and open categories.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, who participated in the 2km Honorary Cup, said Hong Kong should host more major sporting events in future.

"[I am] very glad to have had the opportunity to run on the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge this time. The weather was fantastic and the atmosphere was wonderful,” he said.

“This year's participation also set a new record, so I hope Hong Kong can host more large-scale sports events to showcase our strength, and I hope more members of the general public can take part in these activities."

This year’s event was upgraded to a World Athletics Platinum Label Road Race, marking the first time the city has hosted this level of competition.

Hong Kong, China's top female distance runner, Virginia Lo, said she was honoured to have competed with other world-class athletes.

“Having represented the city in various competitions over the past few years, I’ve actually seen first-hand how incredible they are, I hope I can keep improving and have even more chances to compete alongside them,” she said.

She also noted that the course was scenic and she was able to enjoy the sunrise at the start. But she also said it was quite sunny and windy, making it less than ideal for runners to perform at their best.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Strong current forces organisers' hand in harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Thousands of swimmers took to the water for the annual cross-harbour race on Sunday morning, swimming a one-kilometre course from…
articles.fullText:
Thousands of swimmers took to the water for the annual cross-harbour race on Sunday morning, swimming a one-kilometre course from Wan Chai Golden Bauhinia Square Public Pier to the Avenue of Stars in Tsim Sha Tsui.

However, the race featuring one batch of contestants was cancelled due to strong currents, affecting about 700 participants.

The race drew a total of about 4,000 participants this year, with about 300 people participating in the racing group and 3,700 people registered to take part in the leisure group.

Keith Sin, the overall male champion, said the instructions of this year's race were clearer than last year's, with the navigation buoys ideally placed while the water temperature was comfortable to swim in.

"I have to say the organisers did a great job, while there might not be any obvious changes, those two navigation buoys were really well done," he said.

"They kept us from worrying about where the finish line was before getting in the water, since it's hard to see it from the starting point, navigation buoys are actually super important, so the organisers really nailed it."

The event also featured a leisure group with approximately 3,700 swimmers in four batches.

Ronnie Wong, president of the Hong Kong China Swimming Association, said although they were confident that all contestants could have finished, they decided to cancel the race for the final group due to safety concerns and time limitations.

"We made a decision today regarding the final batch of about 700 swimmers that due to water currents and safety concerns, we have cancelled the last group from racing, and we will refund their registration fees," he said.

Organisers said they would consider giving the affected swimmers priority registration if they want to take part in next year's race.

Organisers also said 135 contestants this year felt unwell, mainly suffering from minor abrasions and cramps.
